records.title: Prompt Caching 201
records.relevance_note: Prompt Caching 201 is a official doc source with details on prompt caching, prefix stability relevant to cost token management.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on cost budget, context, observability.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Prompt caching applies to the exact prompt prefix; the minimum cacheable prefix is 1024 tokens and increases in 128-token increments, and tools plus structured-output schemas are included in the cacheable prefix.
To maximize cache hits, keep static content and tool definitions at the front and volatile content at the end; using allowed_tools prevents changing tool schemas from invalidating the cached prefix.
Using prompt_cache_key improves routing stickiness to machines more likely to hold the warm prefix cache; the guide reports coding-workload cache-hit rates improving from about 60% to 87%.
In a 10,000-request comparison, Flex processing with extended prompt caching and prompt_cache_key achieved an 8.5% higher cache-hit rate and about 23% lower input-token cost than Batch.
The guide recommends monitoring cached_tokens per request plus usage logs and notes that compaction or dropping earlier turns can reduce cache reuse even when semantics stay similar.

§4.4 Use prompt_cache_key to Improve Routing Stickiness, lines 564-570

records.title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform
records.relevance_note: Provider writeup on reducing tool-prefix token overhead without breaking cacheability.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete token counts, on-demand tool loading pattern, and prompt-cache interaction.

claim_snippets.claim_text: MCP tool libraries can consume very large prompt prefixes, with the writeup citing about 72K tokens for 50+ tools and about 134K tokens in Anthropic's internal setup.
A Tool Search Tool can reduce initial tool-related context from about 77K tokens to about 8.7K tokens, an 85% reduction, by loading relevant tools on demand instead of up front.
On Anthropic's internal MCP evaluation, Tool Search improved Claude Opus 4 scores from 49 to 74 and Claude Opus 4.5 scores from 79.5 to 88.1.
Because deferred tools are excluded from the initial prompt and only inserted when selected, the approach reduces context overhead while preserving the cacheability of the stable prefix.

records.title: Agent SDK: prompt cache invalidated every query() — random UUID in Bash tool description
records.relevance_note: Concrete cache-busting failure in a real agent SDK with root-cause detail.
records.reason_included: Shows how tiny prefix instability in tool descriptions multiplies input cost.

claim_snippets.claim_text: A random UUID inserted into the Bash tool description invalidates an otherwise reusable 17K-token cached prefix and causes each follow-up call to pay full cache-write pricing instead of cache-read pricing.
The reported root cause is a per-call temporary settings filename created with crypto.randomUUID() and embedded into the Bash tool's denyWithinAllow description.
Captured API traffic shows different filenames across successive calls and about 16.8K cache_creation_input_tokens with zero cache_read_input_tokens on the follow-up request.
A practical workaround is to normalize the UUID-bearing filename to a fixed all-zero filename before the request reaches the provider API.

claim_locations.locator: Evidence from captured API traffic, lines 217-223; reproduction details, lines 248-253

records.title: HTTP hook intermittently fails with ECONNREFUSED (despite healthy local server) — cache invalidation and wrong tool behavior
records.relevance_note: Real long-context cost spike caused by nondeterministic hook-side text entering the prefix.
records.reason_included: Captures a cache invalidation path outside the model and tool schema layer.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The UserPromptSubmit hook is reported to fail intermittently about 1 in 10 to 20 prompts with ECONNREFUSED even though the local server is healthy and receives no incoming request during the failures.
When the hook alternates between success and failure text, the prefix seen by the model changes and previously cached tokens are invalidated on long sessions.
The reporter states that one cache-invalidation event on a million-context session caused roughly $45 of recomputation cost.

records.title: Context caching | Gemini API
records.relevance_note: Official mechanism spec for implicit and explicit caching, TTL, and usage accounting.
records.reason_included: Directly covers cache policy, billing drivers, and returned usage fields.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Implicit caching is enabled automatically for Gemini 2.5 models, while explicit caching provides guaranteed savings when a reusable prefix should persist across requests.
Explicit caches use a time-to-live, defaulting to one hour, and the cost depends on the size of the cached input and how long it is stored.
Minimum token counts for caching vary by model, cached content must be a prefix, and cached tokens still count against the model's token limits and standard rate limits.
The API returns cached-token information in usage_metadata so clients can measure reuse directly.
Billing for explicit caching combines reduced-rate cached-token usage with cache-storage duration charges plus the usual charges for other input, output, and tool-use tokens.

How explicit caching reduces costs, lines 708-714

records.title: Long context | Gemini API
records.relevance_note: Long context | Gemini API is a official doc source with details on long context, context reuse relevant to cost token management.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on context, cost budget.

claim_snippets.claim_text: For long-context workloads, context caching is the main optimization because repeated queries against the same large context otherwise pay the full repeated input cost on every request.
The guide frames a cost-accuracy tradeoff in which high retrieval accuracy over many pieces of evidence can require many repeated requests, making cache reuse materially important.
When sending long context, the recommended placement is to put the actual query or question at the end of the prompt.
Longer prompts increase time-to-first-token, so unnecessary tokens should be omitted even when the model can technically fit them.

records.title: Gemini thinking | Gemini API
records.exception_reason: Published just outside the primary window and retained for provider documentation on thinking-budget controls and billed reasoning tokens.
records.relevance_note: Official reasoning-token control surface for cost-aware planning.
records.reason_included: Provides explicit knobs and accounting for reasoning-token spend.

claim_snippets.claim_text: For Gemini 2.5, thinkingBudget controls reasoning-token spend; for Gemini 3, thinkingLevel is the intended control and thinkingBudget may lead to unexpected behavior.
Gemini 2.5 Flash family models can disable thinking with 0 and use dynamic thinking with -1, whereas Gemini 2.5 Pro cannot disable thinking.
When thinking is enabled, billed output includes both normal output tokens and thinking tokens, and thoughtsTokenCount exposes the amount of reasoning produced.
Low or disabled thinking is recommended for easy tasks, while more difficult tasks such as coding or math may warrant higher thinking budgets.

records.title: Auto-compaction triggers prematurely due to cache tokens counted as context usage
records.relevance_note: Auto-compaction triggers prematurely due to cache tokens counted as context usage is a issue thread source with details on token accounting, compaction thresholding relevant to cost token management.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on cost budget, context, recovery.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The session token accounting function included cacheRead and cacheWrite tokens in totalTokens, inflating context usage and causing premature auto-compaction triggers.
The report states that 13 of 14 auto-compactions were false alarms, with one example showing 174K computed tokens versus about 118K actual context tokens.
Sessions that previously ran for seven or more hours reportedly began compacting every 11 to 33 minutes after large tool results once the accounting regression was introduced.
The proposed fix is to exclude cacheRead and cacheWrite from context usage calculations and to refresh totalTokens immediately after compaction so thresholds use post-compaction state.
